svg.title: RAID levels versus wide declustered erasure coding
svg.desc: Block layouts for RAID 1, RAID 10, RAID 5, RAID 6 and a declustered erasure-coded pool, with usable capacity and failure tolerance for each.
svg.text: Where the redundancy lives: RAID layouts vs wide erasure coding
Wide erasure coding, declustered (k+m = 4+2 shown across 12 drives; production pools run 8+2 to 146+4)
Traditional RAID rebuilds onto one replacement drive, so rebuild speed is capped by that drive's write bandwidth.
Declustered EC rebuilds into spare space on all survivors, but must read k surviving strips for every strip it reconstructs.
